segments.text: Listen to a talk in a history class.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Petra is an ancient city located in present-day Jordan.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: It was established as early as 312 BC as the capital city of the Nabataean Kingdom.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: The Nabataeans were skilled traders, and Petra became a major trading hub because of its strategic location along caravan routes that linked the east and west.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Petra's architecture is unique because much of it was carved directly into the rose-red cliffs of the region.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: The most famous structure in the city is known as the Treasury, but it is actually a tomb.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: The city also featured a complex system to manage water, including dams, cisterns, and water channels that allowed it to thrive in the arid region.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: These advanced water-engineering structures were crucial for the survival of its inhabitants, given the low amount of moisture that was available naturally.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: In addition to its architectural and engineering feats, Petra is significant for its cultural exchanges.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: As a trading center, it facilitated the exchange of goods, ideas, and customs between diverse peoples.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: This blend of cultures is evident in the various architectural styles seen in the city, which include influences from Greek, Roman, and indigenous Nabataean designs.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Next, we will explore how archaeologists rediscovered Petra in the 19th century.
